messages:
incident-bot: DETECTED: streaming-service-us-west p99 latency breach (auto-threshold). p95=280ms (SLO 150ms), p99=3.6s (SLO 450ms). streaming error ratio +11%. Auto-paging on-call. :rotating_light:
Noah (oncall-sre): I'm up. pulling traces and streaming runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-latency. Starting quick triage.
Noah (oncall-sre): @Pri can you check runtime and any GPU-side anomalies? I'm seeing long tail on TX path for a subset of KV shards.
Pri (eng-runtime): on it. Flame graphs show bursts of stalled GPU kernels and a corresponding backlog in the request scheduler. Affected host: gpu-hot-07.
Sasha (eng-infra): Infra telemetry shows rising correctable ECC counts and intermittent PCIe link resets on gpu-hot-07. sample dmesg:
```[ 210000.123] GPU3: Correctable ECC error at address 0x3ff12
[ 210001.456] pcieport 0000:03:00.0: AER: corrected error, ID 0000
[ 210002.789] sensor: GPU temp spiking to 94C, thermal throttle engaged```
Devon (eng-sre): streaming stalls line up with sessions pinned to KV shard group 14 on that node. Warm cache is available but handoff causes cold misses and tail spikes.
Noah (oncall-sre): ops-lee, any recent infra work?
ops-lee: no recent maintenance. I see fan RPM dropping periodically on BMC, and `nvidia-smi` shows ECC CE counters climbing on GPU3.
Pri (eng-runtime): theory: flaky accelerator (PCIe resets + ECC) -> transient kernel failures -> long running retries -> queue head-of-line blocking -> p99 tail. Suggest: 1) take gpu-hot-07 out of rotation, 2) steer affected shards to warm spares with staged ramp to avoid cache stampede, 3) enable a lower-cost fallback model for streaming for the affected routes while caches rehydrate.
Sasha (eng-infra): agree. I'll cordon the host and set it DRAINING. Command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-hot-07 && kubectl drain gpu-hot-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
Noah (oncall-sre): do it. Devon, can you apply routing with a staged grace window? we want to avoid thundering-warm misses.
Devon (eng-sre): applying staged routing now: `redwoodctl route update --region us-west --avoid-node gpu-hot-07 --fallback-pool warm-reserve --staged-ramp 60s` (applied).
Devon (eng-sre): enabling fallback for `stream-prod` to `rdm-lite-low-bits` with 30s grace: `redwoodctl route set-fallback stream-prod --model rdm-lite-low-bits --grace-period 30s`
Casey (cs): flagging customers. Impact ~2.7% of us-west requests during window. Most affected tenant: Streamly (live captions). Drafting customer note.
Finn (prod-pm): need ETA for mitigation and a short blurb for execs.
Noah (oncall-sre): cordon/drain started. Sasha, collect BMC logs and attach hardware dumps to ticket. ops-lee, mark node as quarantine after drain.
ops-lee: drain complete. Node moved to quarantine: `redwoodctl node set-state gpu-hot-07 quarantined --reason "ecc/pcie/thermal"`. BMC and `dmesg` uploaded.
Pri (eng-runtime): immediate metrics: after routing changes p95=160ms, p99=580ms and trending downward. Streaming stall ratio dropped from 4.3% -> 0.9%. KV miss spike happened during handoff but warmed over ~3 minutes.
Devon (eng-sre): routing flush confirmed. tail latency decaying.
Sasha (eng-infra): opening vendor case, collecting full logs and power telemetry. suspicion: intermittent fan PWM driver + PCIe lane flakiness. ticket: VEND-96245.
Noah (oncall-sre): severity: Sev2 (partial). timeline: detected at 1999990000; mitigations (routing + fallback + drain) in place by 1999990280.
Casey (cs): notified Streamly support. They reported caption jitter for ~5m, now stable on fallback model. Message: "We've routed your traffic to unaffected capacity with a temporary model fallback while we investigate a hardware issue."
Finn (prod-pm): added incident to tracker. Please capture any temporary config flags and the rollout diff.
Pri (eng-runtime): follow-up action: I'll add a preemptive runtime policy to mark GPUs with rapid PCIe/AER or CE spikes for soft-drain if threshold exceeded (configurable). Will open PR referencing this incident and include telemetry tests.
Devon (eng-sre): created a temporary alert `gpu-aer-spike-action` to make the event actionable sooner.
Sasha (eng-infra): vendor indicates RMA likely if errors persist. arranging replacement window and on-site swap.
Noah (oncall-sre): handing to Devon for overnight monitoring and to coordinate with infra on RMA. Devon, own post-incident checklist and customer follow-ups.
Noah (oncall-sre): handoff notes: mitigations applied (staged routing, fallback model, node drained). p95 returned near SLO; p99 slightly elevated but trending down. no open escalations beyond Streamly monitoring.
Devon (eng-sre): ack. will watch alerts, ensure warm pool healthy, and coordinate with Sasha on replacement. assigning follow-ups: runtime guard PR (Pri), infra RMA (Sasha), customer comms (Casey), PM write-up (Finn). closing active pager. :white_check_mark:
Noah (oncall-sre): switching incident status to monitoring.
Devon (eng-sre): final note: impact window and request counts logged. will reopen if regression observed.
Noah (oncall-sre): oncall handoff at 1999990455.
